insights.headline: Gold and silver held near record highs as festive buying began, even as a hawkish Fed kept global prices under pressure.
insights.summary: Indian buyers head into the festive season with 24K gold near ₹1.53 lakh per 10 grams in major cities. On MCX, gold October futures ended the week at ₹1,51,135 and silver December futures at ₹2,33,850 after hawkish US Fed signals and multi-decade Treasury yields pressured global bullion. Kotak flagged downside risk to its FY27 gold-import forecast after the duty hike to 15%, while China's record gold imports and the RBI's rising gold reserves offered a counterweight.
points: Delhi 24K gold was ₹1,52,820 per 10g on Sept 27 and Mumbai ₹1,52,670, with 22K near ₹1.40 lakh.
MCX gold October futures closed at ₹1,51,135 (−2% weekly); silver December at ₹2,33,850 (−2%).
Gold import duty rose to 15% from 6%; Kotak sees downside risk to its $88 billion FY27 import forecast.
RBI's gold reserves rose $68 million to $111.29 billion even as forex reserves fell $14.9 billion.
China imported a record $158.8 billion of gold (over 1,100 tonnes) in the first eight months of 2026.

items.title: Gold Rate Today, September 27, 2026: Check 22K and 24K Gold Prices in Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Other Cities
items.summary: Retail gold rates held near record levels on September 27. In Delhi, 22K gold cost ₹1,40,090 and 24K ₹1,52,820 per 10 grams, while Mumbai listed 22K at ₹1,39,940 and 24K at ₹1,52,670. Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad stayed in the same band, with small regional differences from local taxes and transport costs.

items.title: Gold Slides 2% to $4,288; Silver Falls 3.7% to $63.90 on Hawkish Fed, Stronger Dollar and Rising Yields
items.summary: Spot gold fell over 2% in the week ended September 25 to settle near $4,288 an ounce, while spot silver lost nearly 3.7% to $63.90, as hawkish Fed commentary, a firmer dollar and multi-decade-high Treasury yields outweighed safe-haven demand. On MCX, gold October futures closed at ₹1,51,135 per 10 grams, down about 2% weekly, and silver December futures settled at ₹2,33,850 per kg, down nearly 2%.

items.title: Kotak sees downside risk to FY27 gold-import forecast after sharp monthly decline
items.summary: Kotak flagged downside risk to its $88 billion FY27 gold-import forecast after a sharp monthly decline, following the rise in import duty from 6% to 15%. The note says festive demand could partly offset weaker volumes, but expects imports to stay under pressure while the higher duty holds.

items.title: India's forex fall by $14.9 billion in a week, says RBI: Where do reserves stand now?
items.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $14.9 billion in a week to $765.9 billion, the RBI's latest weekly data show. Within the reserves, the central bank's gold holdings rose $68 million to $111.29 billion, underscoring how bullion continues to anchor India's external buffers even as the rupee stays under pressure.

items.title: ICICI Bank sees gold consolidating through 2026 before firming in H1 2027
items.summary: ICICI Bank expects gold to consolidate at high levels through the rest of 2026 after a sharp September correction, blaming a hawkish repricing of US monetary policy, higher oil prices and strong labour data. The bank points to $17.8 billion of August ETF inflows and the People's Bank of China's 20-tonne August purchase as structural supports for bullion.

items.title: Gold Falls 5th Week Running as AI Tech Spending Surges
items.summary: London gold fell 1.8% week-on-week to about $4,268 an ounce, a fifth straight weekly decline, as heavy AI-related tech spending pulled money toward equities. Silver lost 5.3% on the week to below $63.50, while the US 10-year Treasury yield pushed above 5.20%, raising the cost of holding bullion.

items.title: Wall Street split on gold price path after drop below $4,300, Main Street maintains bullish majority as jobs take center stage
items.summary: Wall Street analysts are split on gold's near-term path after prices fell below $4,300, while Main Street investors keep a bullish majority. The survey shows attention shifting to upcoming US jobs data, which could shape expectations for the Federal Reserve's next rate move.

items.title: Gold Futures Snap Four-day Losing Streak To Close Higher On Better COMEX Performance
items.summary: Malaysian gold futures rebounded with COMEX, snapping a four-day losing streak, with the September contract closing at $4,292.40. The bounce tracked a firmer overnight US session as buyers returned after the week's rate-driven selloff.
